root.docs:
FHIR R4 endpoints. Base URL: {{fhirBaseUrl}} = https://api.preview.platform.athenahealth.com/fhir/r4

FHIR APIs are standards-based and free (no per-call cost). However, they are largely read-only — write-back requires proprietary athenaOne endpoints.

All FHIR requests use `Accept: application/fhir+json`.

Required OAuth scopes for Subscriptions: `system/SubscriptionTopic.read`, `system/Subscription.write`, `system/Subscription.read`.

request.docs:
**Juno Use Case:** Subscribe to Encounter.signoff events. When a provider signs off on an encounter, Athena sends an `id-only` event notification to Juno's webhook. Juno then calls `GET /chart/encounter/{id}/summary` to pull the encounter content.

**Delivery:** `id-only` payload — each notification contains only the resource ID. A follow-up API call is required to fetch content (this is Athena's pattern for all FHIR subscriptions).

**Webhook requirements:**
- HTTPS on port 443
- 2-second hard response timeout (must return 200 immediately; process async)
- At-least-once delivery with deduplication IDs

**Required scopes:** `system/SubscriptionTopic.read`, `system/Subscription.write`

**Other subscribable events:** `Encounter.check-in`, `Encounter.reopen`, `PatientProblem.create/update/delete`, `Prescription.create/update`, `LabResult.create/update/close`, `Patient.create/update/merge`, `PatientCase.create/update/add-note`, `Appointment.schedule/check-in/check-out/cancel`

**Alpha topics:** `ClinicalDocument.create/update`, `AdminDocument.create/update`, `MedicalRecord`, `PatientInfoOrder`, `Letter`

**GitHub:** https://github.com/athenahealth/aone-fhir-subscriptions

**Replace `endpoint` value** with your actual Juno webhook URL before use.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Standards-based retrieval of a specific clinical document by FHIR ID.

**Key fields:** `content.attachment.url` or `content.attachment.data` (document content), `type` (LOINC code for note type), `category`, `subject` (patient ref), `author` (provider), `date`, `context.encounter`.

**Athena extension:** `ahPublishedDateTimeToPortal` — tells Juno when documents were shared with the patient.

**Profile:** Athena's `ah-documentreference` profile (https://fhir.athena.io/athenacoreext/StructureDefinition-ah-documentreference.html).

**FHIR Subscription:** `ClinicalDocument.create` [Alpha] triggers on new clinical docs.

**Juno Use Case:** List all active FHIR Subscriptions for the current app. Use to inspect registered webhooks, check subscription status, and audit what events Juno is subscribed to.

**Required scope:** `system/Subscription.read`

**GitHub reference:** https://github.com/athenahealth/aone-fhir-subscriptions

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** FHIR-standard retrieval of patient demographics. Returns a FHIR Patient resource with name, DOB, address, contact info, preferred language.

**Proprietary alternative:** `GET /v1/{{practiceId}}/patients/{{patientId}}` (MEDIUM priority folder) — may include more Athena-specific fields.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** FHIR-standard retrieval of the patient's allergy list. Returns a Bundle of AllergyIntolerance resources.

**Proprietary alternative:** `GET /v1/{{practiceId}}/chart/{{patientId}}/allergies` (MEDIUM priority folder).

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Retrieve any structured care plans filed against the patient as context for Juno's output.

**Note:** CarePlan support added as part of ONC HTI-1 Final Rule compliance (USCDI). Data is likely thin in ambulatory workflows but may grow over time. Read-only in Athena's FHIR API.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** FHIR-standard retrieval of the patient's problem list / diagnoses. Returns a Bundle of Condition resources with ICD-10 codes.

**FHIR Subscription:** `PatientProblem` topic supports `create`, `update`, `delete` events.

**Proprietary alternative:** `GET /v1/{{practiceId}}/chart/{{patientId}}/problems` (HIGH priority folder).

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Search for all clinical documents for a patient using FHIR. Returns a Bundle of DocumentReference resources.

This is the FHIR-standard alternative to the proprietary `GET /patients/{id}/documents` endpoint. Preferred if Juno uses SMART on FHIR app launch.

**Key search params:** `patient`, `type` (LOINC code), `date`, `_count`.

**Athena extension:** `ahPublishedDateTimeToPortal` on each DocumentReference shows when docs were shared with the patient.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** FHIR-standard retrieval of immunization history. Important for neurology patients on immunosuppressive therapies (e.g., MS biologics and live vaccine contraindications).

**Proprietary alternative:** `GET /v1/{{practiceId}}/chart/{{patientId}}/immunizations` (LOW priority folder).

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** FHIR-standard retrieval of active medications. Returns a Bundle of MedicationRequest resources with RxNorm codes, dosage, and instructions.

**FHIR Subscription:** `Prescription` topic supports `create`, `update`, `refill-create` events.

**Proprietary alternative:** `GET /v1/{{practiceId}}/chart/{{patientId}}/medications` (HIGH priority folder).

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Retrieve procedures (e.g., nerve block, infusion, biopsy) as context for Juno's post-procedure care guidance.

**Note:** Returns FHIR Procedure resources with CPT/SNOMED codes and dates.

root.docs: Authentication endpoints. Use 'Get Token' to manually obtain an access token. The collection-level pre-request script handles automatic token refresh for all other requests.

request.docs:
Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token using the client_credentials grant. The token is valid for a limited duration (typically 3600 seconds). The response `access_token` and `expires_in` are stored into env vars by the test script below.

Credentials are sent as HTTP Basic Auth (Base64-encoded `clientId:clientSecret`).

You typically do not need to run this manually — the collection pre-request script auto-refreshes the token. Run this directly only to debug authentication issues.

root.docs:
Run these requests in order to discover IDs from just a practiceId. Copy IDs from responses into the environment variables (departmentId, patientId, encounterId, etc.) so all other requests work.

Order: Departments → Providers → Patients → Booked Appointments → Encounter Summary

See GETTING-STARTED.md for the full walkthrough with curl examples.

request.docs:
Discovers all department IDs. No prerequisites — works with just practiceId + token.

Copy a `departmentid` from the response into the `departmentId` environment variable.

Lists providers for the practice. No prerequisites.

Copy a `providerid` from the response into the `providerId` environment variable.

Lists pre-seeded patients in the sandbox practice. No prerequisites.

Copy a `patientid` from the response into the `patientId` environment variable.

Optionally enable the firstname/lastname/dob query params to search for a specific patient.

Tip: Try patientId=1 in the next request — used in the go-athenahealth SDK as a hello-world call.

Fetch full demographics for a patient. Requires `patientId` env var — run '3. List Patients' first and copy an ID.

Tip: Try patientId=1 first (go-athenahealth SDK hello-world example).

The most efficient bootstrap call — each appointment in the response contains `appointmentid`, `patientid`, `departmentid`, AND `encounterid` in one shot.

Copy values into the corresponding environment variables:
- `appointmentid` → `appointmentId`
- `encounterid` → `encounterId` (look for one where encounterid is not null/0 — means visit was completed)
- `patientid` → `patientId`
- `departmentid` → `departmentId`

If no results: widen the date range. If `encounterid` is null: the appointment was booked but patient never checked out — those won't have encounter summaries.

Juno's primary PULL endpoint. Requires `encounterId` — run '4. List Booked Appointments' and copy an encounterId where the value is non-null.

Key field in response: `summaryhtml` — the full clinician narrative as HTML (HPI, assessment, plan, orders). This feeds Juno's translation pipeline.

Note: path is /chart/encounter/ not /appointments/ — different branch of the API.

**Subscribe first:** `POST /v1/{{practiceId}}/patients/changed/subscription` to register.

request.docs:
**Juno Use Case (PUSH):** Attach a Juno-generated plain-language summary as a clinical document to the patient's chart, visible to the care team.

**Key fields:**
- `attachmentcontents`: Base64-encoded file data
- `attachmenttype`: MIME type (application/pdf, text/html, text/plain)
- `departmentid`: Required — department where doc is filed
- `documentsubclass`: Document subclass label
- `internalnote`: Note visible to care team in Athena UI

**Note:** Subscription event `ClinicalDocument.create/update` (Alpha) can notify Juno when new clinical documents are filed. Verify accepted `documentsubclass` values with Athena during onboarding.

request.docs:
**Juno Use Case (PUSH):** Create a Patient Case note visible to the care team logging that Juno sent a plain-language summary to the patient. Include the Juno link and engagement metrics (viewed, completed checklist, etc.) to close the loop for the provider.

**Key fields:**
- `note`: Note text (include Juno URL and engagement status)
- `departmentid`: Required
- `patientid`: Required

**FHIR Subscription events:** `PatientCase.create`, `PatientCase.update`, `PatientCase.add-note` — Juno can listen for provider replies to the Patient Case.

**Advantage:** Low-friction write-back that doesn't require Athena approval for a new document class.

request.docs:
[PATH UNVERIFIED - CHECK ATHENA DOCS]

**Juno Use Case (PUSH):** Send a secure portal message to the patient containing the Juno plain-language care link, enabling the patient to access personalized care guidance directly from the Athena patient portal (athenaPatient).

**Key fields:** `messagetext` (body), `subject`, `patientid`, `departmentid`. Thread ID for replies.

**Critical open question:** Does the Athena Patient Portal render hyperlinks in message bodies as clickable? Test in sandbox — if not, fall back to plain URL text or embed summary content directly.

**Note:** Exact endpoint path must be confirmed at docs.athenahealth.com/api/api-ref/secure-messages. FHIR Subscription event `PatientCase.add-note` can track provider responses.

**Juno Use Case (PULL — trigger mechanism):** Poll for encounters that have changed since the last poll. This is the legacy pull-based alternative to FHIR Event Subscriptions for detecting `Encounter.signoff` events.

Use this for practices that do not support the FHIR Subscription framework, or as a fallback when webhook delivery fails.

**Polling latency:** 1–5 minutes depending on interval. Subscribe with `POST /v1/{{practiceId}}/encounters/changed/subscription` before polling.

**Preferred alternative:** FHIR Subscription `Encounter.signoff` event (real-time, ~seconds latency) — see FHIR R4 folder.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Retrieve an existing clinical document as CCD/CCDA XML. Useful for ingesting structured clinical data from discharge summaries or external records.

The C-CDA XML format is rich in structured clinical data (medications, problems, allergies, results) and may be more complete than individual chart endpoints.

**Response format:** CCD/CCDA XML (not JSON). Set Accept header to `application/xml`.

**See also:** `FHIR - Get DocumentReference` for the FHIR-standard equivalent.

[PATH UNVERIFIED - CHECK ATHENA DOCS]

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** For clinic practices that handle hospital admissions (neurology inpatient cases), retrieve discharge instructions and discharge summary text for translation into Juno's plain-language guidance.

**Key fields (expected):** Discharge instructions text, discharge date, follow-up instructions, discharge diagnosis.

**Action required:** Verify exact endpoint path at docs.athenahealth.com/api/api-ref/discharge-info. This endpoint may only be available to practices with hospital integration modules (not standard ambulatory). Confirm during sandbox testing.

**Companion endpoint:** `Hospital Systems Visit` at docs.athenahealth.com/api/api-ref/hospital-systems-visit covers inpatient visit context.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Retrieve the complete clinician encounter write-up (HPI, exam, assessment and plan, orders) after a visit is signed off. The `summaryhtml` field is the primary input for Juno's translation pipeline.

**Key field:** `summaryhtml` — entire encounter summary as HTML including HPI, physical exam, assessment and plan, and orders. Confirmed via go-athenahealth SDK (`EncounterSummaryResponse.Summary` → `summaryhtml`).

**Trigger:** Call this endpoint upon receiving an `Encounter.signoff` FHIR Subscription event (see FHIR R4 folder).

**Note:** This is the single richest text endpoint for Juno's PULL pipeline. Data completeness depends on the provider's template.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Pull the patient's current medication list to include in Juno's plain-language care guidance. Critical for neurology patients (MS, Parkinson's, dementia) where medication adherence is central to care.

**Key fields:** Medication name, dosage, frequency, instructions, prescriber, start/stop dates, status (active/inactive), RxNorm code.

**FHIR alternative:** `GET {{fhirBaseUrl}}/MedicationRequest?patient={{patientId}}` (see FHIR R4 folder).

**Change polling:** `GET /v1/{{practiceId}}/prescriptions/changed` for polling-based change detection. FHIR Subscription topic `Prescription` supports events: `create`, `update`, `refill-create`.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Pull the patient's active problem list (ICD-10 diagnoses) to personalize Juno's plain-language care guidance — e.g., tailor MS relapse content specifically for the patient's documented MS subtype.

**Key fields:** Problem name, ICD-10 code, onset date, status (active/inactive), notes, provider.

**FHIR alternative:** `GET {{fhirBaseUrl}}/Condition?patient={{patientId}}` (see FHIR R4 folder).

**Change polling:** `ListChangedProblems` endpoint. FHIR Subscription topic `PatientProblem` supports `create`, `update`, `delete` events.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** List all documents in a patient's chart. Use this to discover available clinical documents (discharge summaries, external notes, C-CDA documents) for ingestion into Juno's pipeline.

Optionally filter by `documentclass` to narrow results. For example, `documentclass=CLINICALDOCUMENT` returns only clinical documents; `documentclass=ENCOUNTERDOCUMENT` returns encounter-specific documents.

**Note:** The generic `POST /documents` endpoint was retired in 2016; use class-specific endpoints for document creation.

request.docs:
**Juno Use Case (PUSH):** Send a Juno-generated plain-language care letter (formatted for patient readability) as a Letter document. Athena can deliver this via portal, print-to-mail, or patient-facing communication.

**Key fields:** `attachmentcontents` (base64), `attachmenttype`, `departmentid`, `providerid`.

**Open question:** Confirm whether Athena allows hyperlinks within letter bodies for Juno's URL-based delivery model.

**Note:** Letters in Athena can be routed to the patient portal or printed — this is a supported formal delivery channel.

[PATH UNVERIFIED - CHECK ATHENA DOCS]

**Juno Use Case (PUSH):** Post a Juno-generated structured note as an office note subtype if clinical workflows require it. May also be used to PULL provider-dictated office notes (separate from auto-generated encounter summaries).

**Note:** Separate from the generic Clinical Document class. Verify accepted fields and exact path at docs.athenahealth.com/api/api-ref/document-type-office-note.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Pull allergy list to include safety context in Juno's medication-related plain-language guidance.

**Key fields:** Allergen name, reaction, severity, onset date.

**FHIR alternative:** `GET {{fhirBaseUrl}}/AllergyIntolerance?patient={{patientId}}` (see FHIR R4 folder).

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Pull any notes attached to an appointment — may contain pre-existing patient instructions or provider notes that provide context for Juno's pipeline.

**Note:** Confirm field structure and available note types at docs.athenahealth.com/api/api-ref/appointment-notes.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Pull appointment context (type, provider, department, date) to pre-populate Juno's pipeline context before the encounter summary is signed.

**Key fields:** Appointment type, provider ID, department ID, patient ID, date/time, appointment status.

**FHIR Subscription:** `Appointment` topic supports `schedule`, `check-in`, `check-out`, `cancel`, `reschedule` events. The `Appointment.check-out` event can serve as an alternative trigger to `Encounter.signoff`.

**Juno Use Case (PULL — legacy polling):** Poll for encounters that have changed since last poll. Alternative to FHIR Subscriptions for practices without webhook support.

This is a duplicate of the HIGH priority 'Get Changed Encounters' request, listed here for completeness under the Changed Data Subscriptions category.

**Changed Data feed types (verified):** patients, appointments, lab results, prescriptions, problems, providers, clinical documents.

**Subscribe first:** `POST /v1/{{practiceId}}/encounters/changed/subscription` to register for polling.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Access structured encounter service notes (SOAP note sections) as a supplement or alternative to the full `summaryhtml` endpoint. May expose finer-grained sections (HPI, ROS, physical exam, A&P) separately rather than as a single HTML blob.

**Note:** Verify field-level structure at docs.athenahealth.com/api/api-ref/encounter-chart. Athena supports vitals, screening questionnaires, diagnosis, history, and physical examination sections — these may be structured fields rather than free text, enabling more targeted extraction.

**Complement with:** `GET /v1/{{practiceId}}/chart/encounter/{{encounterId}}/summary` (HIGH priority) for the full HTML summary.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Retrieve recent lab results to include in Juno's care guidance — especially for MS patients (MRI results, JC virus titers) or Parkinson's patients where results drive care instructions.

**Key fields:** Test name, LOINC code, value, units, reference range, abnormal flag, collection date.

**FHIR alternatives:** `DiagnosticReport` and `Observation` resources also provide lab data.

**FHIR Subscription:** `LabResult` topic supports `create`, `update`, `close` events. `ListChangedLabResults` for polling.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Retrieve patient information / education orders placed by providers during the encounter. These may contain specific care instruction text or references to educational materials that Juno should amplify and translate.

**Key fields:** Order type (patient info/education), order text, instructions text, provider, encounter reference.

**FHIR Subscription:** `PatientInfoOrder` topic [Alpha] — events: `create`, `update`, `delete`.

**Note:** This is the closest Athena API surface to 'patient instructions' explicitly embedded in the clinical order workflow. Verify exact endpoint path at docs.athenahealth.com/api/api-ref/order-patient-info-order.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Read practice-specific custom fields configured by the clinic (e.g., 'preferred caregiver contact', 'Juno consent given', 'last Juno link sent') for workflow tracking and personalization.

**PUSH version:** See 'Update Patient Custom Fields' in the LOW priority folder.

**Note:** Custom fields are practice-specific — the available fields depend on what each clinic has configured in their Athena instance.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Get patient demographics to personalize Juno's plain-language content delivery — especially important for neurology patients where a caregiver may be the primary recipient.

**Key fields:** First name, last name, DOB, preferred language, email, phone, caregiver/guarantor info, portal enrollment status.

**FHIR alternative:** `GET {{fhirBaseUrl}}/Patient/{{patientId}}` (see FHIR R4 folder).

**FHIR Subscription:** `Patient` topic supports `create`, `update`, `delete`, `merge` events. `ListChangedPatients` available for polling.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** List booked appointments for a department/date range. Useful for scheduling-aware workflows (e.g., pre-loading patient context before encounters, or batch-sending care summaries for appointments that day).

**Key params:** `departmentid`, `startdate`, `enddate` (MM/DD/YYYY format), `providerid`.

**FHIR Subscription:** `Appointment` topic — `ListChangedAppointments` for polling.

**Juno Use Case (PULL):** Retrieve documents attached directly to an encounter (external referral docs, imaging reports, specialist notes attached to visit) that may add clinical context for Juno's pipeline.

This is the same endpoint as 'List Patient Documents' (HIGH priority) but filtered with `documentclass=ENCOUNTERDOCUMENT`.

**SDK reference:** `ListEncounterDocuments(ctx, departmentID, patientID, opts)` confirmed in go-athenahealth SDK.

**Note:** Verify available document classes at docs.athenahealth.com/api/api-ref/document-type-encounter-document.

**Juno Use Case:** Search/list patients by name, DOB, or department. Useful for patient lookup during testing and during Juno onboarding flows where a provider selects a patient to send a care summary.

**Key query params:** `lastname`, `firstname`, `dob` (MM/DD/YYYY), `departmentid`, `limit`.

**FHIR Subscription:** `Patient` topic supports `create`, `update`, `delete`, `merge` events.

root.docs:
Postman collection for the Athena Health API (sandbox) covering all endpoints relevant to the Juno integration. Includes proprietary athenaOne REST APIs (v1) and FHIR R4 endpoints.

**Sandbox base URL:** https://api.preview.platform.athenahealth.com
**Default practice ID:** 195900 (ambulatory sandbox)

**Setup:**
1. Import the companion environment file `athena-health-sandbox.postman_environment.json`
2. Set `clientId` and `clientSecret` in the environment
3. Optionally run 'Auth > Get Token' once, or let the collection pre-request script handle it automatically

**Quick start:** Run "Bootstrap / Discovery" in order — copy IDs from responses into env vars (departmentId, patientId, encounterId) so all other requests work immediately.

**Authentication:** OAuth 2.0 client_credentials. The collection-level pre-request script auto-refreshes the access token before expiry so you don't need to manually re-authenticate.
